assessment.security_status_cs: Región Asie-Pacifik čelí rostoucímu napětí v oblasti kosmické bezpečnosti a námořních tras (Somálské pirátství, Jihočínské moře), zatímco Čína diplomaticky manévruje před summitem Xi-Trump z pozice síly. Domácí ekonomika a korporátní sféra se mezitím přizpůsobují novým ekonomickým plánům Hong Kongu a rostoucímu tlaku protikorupčních úřadů.
assessment.security_status_en: The Asia-Pacific region faces rising tensions in space security and maritime corridors (Somali piracy, South China Sea), while China maneuvers diplomatically ahead of the Xi-Trump summit from a position of strength. Domestically, the corporate sphere is adapting to Hong Kong's new economic plans and tightening anti-corruption enforcement.

articles.title: Hong Kong’s first 5-year plan to give firms more long-term certainty: Paul Chan
articles.summary:
Hong Kong’s first five-year plan will give businesses greater certainty to make long-term investment decisions amid a volatile external environment, the city’s finance chief has said.
Financial Secretary Paul Chan Mo-po said the plan’s targets and timelines would allow companies to see the city’s direction over the next five years and better align their plans with the government’s.

articles.title: Chinese firms keen on investing in Oman’s International Financial Centre: official
articles.summary:
Chinese firms have shown “very strong interest” in investing in Oman – across the Strait of Hormuz from Iran – as they aim to tap the lucrative Middle East market while minimising risks, an Omani official said.
Banks, asset managers and law firms from China were getting in touch every day to ask about setting up in the International Financial Centre Oman, a free-standing legal zone in the country, the centre’s associate director for business development, Al Hussain al-Qalhati, said.

articles.title: The cooling trap: how Asia’s air conditioners are making heatwaves worse
articles.summary:
As heatwaves become more frequent and intense across Asia, the region faces a dangerous power paradox. Soaring demand for air conditioning threatens to push electricity grids closer to failure just as extreme heat puts the infrastructure under greater strain, raising the risk of cooling disappearing when people need it most.
That risk has been visible across the region this summer.

articles.title: Chinese man sues AI firm after chatbot’s ‘auspicious’ date suggestion leads to disaster
articles.summary:
A man in eastern China filed a lawsuit against an AI company after he followed a chatbot’s recommendation for his mother’s burial date, which he later claimed was linked to a family misfortune.
According to Jimu News, Shi, from Jiashan county in Zhejiang province, lost his mother to a sudden illness in April.

articles.title: Chinese lawyers offer coaching for when corruption busters come knocking
articles.summary:
Zhang Dongdong has been fielding ever more requests for legal advice from jittery entrepreneurs, nervous government officials or their desperate relatives.
They usually do not tell him the whole story, and sometimes say it happened “to a friend”, but most want to know the same thing: what to do when they are targeted by China’s corruption busters.

articles.title: What Hong Kong cinema can take away from a popular Chinese war film
articles.summary:
In late August, I took my parents to see Once Upon a Time in the Middle East in their small-town cinema on the mainland. Built around an unnamed conflict widely understood to be the US-led Iraq war, the film has become the kind of phenomenon no marketing budget could buy, projected to reach 2.5 billion yuan (US$372.5 million) largely through word of mouth.

articles.title: Xi sends condolences as Hong Kong’s first chief executive Tung Chee-hwa honoured in state funeral
articles.summary:
Hong Kong is bidding farewell to its first post-colonial chief executive, Tung Chee-hwa, on Sunday at a state funeral – only the third time a Hongkonger has received such an honour since the 1997 handover.
Tung, who died at the age of 89 on September 8, led Hong Kong through a series of ups and downs, including the 1997 Asian financial crisis, the 2003 Sars outbreak and the V-shaped economic recovery that followed.

articles.title: Analysts tip a stronger hand for China ahead of Xi-Trump summit in Washington
articles.summary:
When the presidents of the United States and China meet in Washington, the world will be watching to see whether their two countries can make good on their agreement to work towards “constructive strategic stability”. In the second part of a series, Fan Chen looks at Beijing’s stronger position going into the high-stakes visit.
Beijing is poised to begin this week’s summit with Washington from a position of strength, bolstered by a flurry of recent diplomatic outreach.

articles.title: What China really means when it says it’s being ‘strategic’
articles.summary:
On September 12, Chinese President Xi Jinping met Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi on the sidelines of the Brics summit in New Delhi. In their talks, Xi said China approached the relationship “from a strategic and long-term perspective”.
He called for an objective and rational “strategic” perception. That means the two sides should treat each other as partners rather than rivals, and as opportunities rather than threats.

articles.summary:
US President Donald Trump ⁠said in a social media post ⁠on Saturday that he plans to appoint a new artificial intelligence adviser, known as an “AI tsar”, and create an “AI force”, though he did not provide details about either initiative or how they would be implemented.

articles.title: Hong Kong’s political, business elite pay final respects to Tung Chee-hwa
articles.summary:
Hong Kong’s political and business elite bade a solemn farewell to Tung Chee-hwa, the city’s first chief executive, at a vigil on Saturday, as Beijing leaders sent wreaths ahead of his state funeral and members of the public streamed into community centres to sign condolence books.

articles.title: Is China’s fabled Empress Dowager Huayang buried near an airport? A study says yes
articles.summary:
An airport is an unlikely place to search for national origins but researchers say they have uncovered the tomb of the woman behind the man who unified China – next to a major city runway.
The researchers said the tomb was believed to belong to Empress Dowager Huayang, the adoptive grandmother of Qin Shi Huang, who unified the warring states more than 2,200 years ago.

articles.title: In a first, top European design prize awarded to €20 uniform for China’s delivery drivers
articles.summary:
Taobao Instant Commerce, Alibaba’s on-demand delivery service that was revamped last year and is known as Taobao Shangou in Chinese, won a top French Design Award prize on Saturday for its delivery worker uniform, marking the first time the prize was awarded for a design for frontline workers.

articles.title: Somali piracy rise tests China’s long-running Gulf of Aden mission
articles.summary:
For more than a decade, China has deployed warships to the Gulf of Aden and the waters off Somalia.
For much of that time, piracy in the region has been in sharp decline. Now, however, with attacks at their highest reported level since 2013 and other naval forces engaged in crises elsewhere, Beijing’s long-running escort mission is being tested.

articles.title: US space weapons move has ‘broken taboo’, could spark new arms race, Beijing forum told
articles.summary:
The US deployment of space weapons has shattered a long-held taboo and risks igniting a fresh arms race, with the world at a “breaking point in history”, speakers at a major security conference in Beijing have warned.
Experts at the Xiangshan Forum this week also called for US-China dialogue on space security, just days before Chinese President Xi Jinping makes his first state visit to the US in more than a decade.

articles.title: China-led study reveals ‘Greater Gondwana’ was 80% of Earth’s crust 500m years ago
articles.summary:
Fragments of a long-disappeared ancient giant land mass have been discovered buried deep beneath parts of the modern continents that once formed it, according to an international team led by Chinese scientists.
Published this month in the peer-reviewed journal Science Advances, the discovery reveals that Gondwana – a land mass that dominated Earth some 500 million years ago – was much larger than previously believed.

articles.title: Customs seizes record HK$125 million worth of marijuana shipped by sea, arresting 3
articles.summary:
Customs has made the largest seizure of drugs shipped by sea in Hong Kong’s history, discovering HK$125 million (US$15.93 million) worth of marijuana in a 40-foot container and arresting three people.
The Customs and Excise Department revealed on Saturday that it had selected a seaborne container at the Kwai Chung Customhouse Cargo Examination Compound for inspection earlier in September after conducting a risk assessment and intelligence analysis.

articles.title: Cathay Pacific retains third-best airline title, wins cabin crew and lounge awards
articles.summary:
Hong Kong flag carrier Cathay Pacific Airways has been ranked the world’s third-best airline for the second consecutive year, while also taking top awards for best cabin crew and first-class lounge in new industry rankings.
Singapore Airlines reclaimed the top spot in the British-based Skytrax World Airline Awards, moving up from second place last year and swapping positions with Qatar Airways, which dropped to second.

articles.title: Hong Kong police arrest 3, seize HK$23 million of Ice in Fanling bust
articles.summary:
Police have arrested three people and broken up a large-scale drug production factory in northern Hong Kong, seizing HK$23 million (US$3 million) worth of suspected methamphetamine, or Ice.
The force said on Saturday that two men and a woman, aged 49 to 56, were arrested on Thursday night.
Police in Fanling first intercepted one of the men, who was holding a two-way permit, a document issued by mainland Chinese authorities allowing residents to travel to Hong Kong.

articles.summary:
In China, an increasing number of digital face-licensing platforms are connecting ordinary individuals with content creators, enabling them to authorise the use of their likenesses in AI-generated short dramas, advertisements, and games.
Since April, private “face-selling” transactions that once circulated within film and television industry chat groups have progressively transitioned to public platforms.
